Alison Botha Re-visited

By: Michael Duffett | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The trauma re-visited

Summary:
Many viewers will remember the story 20 years ago of the bravery of Alison Botha who was raped, stabbed repeatedly and had her throat so severely cut that she was almost decapitated. Her rapist, along with an accomplice, who was out on bail already for two other rapes, was sentenced to three life sentences with the judge wanting him never to see the light of day again.
Such was the resilience of Alison that she survived, recovered and went on to become a motivational speaker. Now a film is about to be made on her and it was during the research for this film that some rather disturbing news has emerged...
• Frans, her rapist, is having an internet based relationship with someone on the outside.
• The filmmaker was horrified to find that a warder of his started to communicate with her via Whatsapp.
• Facebook exchanges show that wardens know about Frans's access to the internet/Facebook and chat rooms.
• It seems that this man may be up for parole.
• When Alison complained to authorities about Frans having internet access and asked for her complaint to be kept confidential, it seems that the prison head went straight to Frans with her complaint. Alison is furious about this and her name now is being thrown around by Frans in his Facebook exchanges.



Further information:
The story is about a recap of the brutal experience suffered by Alison. Her inspirational tale moved a local filmmaker who has decided to make a film about her. In her research, and when she contacted all the role players, she discovered everything that is written above. Alison feels compromised. It seems that correctional services have acted with extreme stupidity. One of the questions we need to look at once again during this program is the possibility that those convicted of the most heinous crimes could be getting parole. A question we must ask, is there any crime committed that is so horrific and evil that there is no chance of them ever leaving prison. Frans would seem to fit this picture. The story will leave the viewer feeling this... woman who survives her horrific ordeal and manages to rebuild her life. She now is compromised by the inept actions of correctional services.

AMALIA EMAIL TO MIKE: 20.4.2015

Herewith our notes - and Laura’s below which she also sent to you directly. thank you! please let me know what the lawyers said:

1. The beginning needed some context give more context – the hint of what was to come needs to be better written to explain.
2. Rather start the story with the actual event – go straight into the rape, recap the original story but make it feel like you are telling that story as though its current, then come to the present and reflect back on the past.
3. The recap of Alison’s original story can be reduced
4. You need to pull out and type the words on screen from the whats app chats every time we see them and zoom in much more to show only the sections you are referring to.
5. Slit her throat 16 times – what does this mean – don’t you only slit a throat once?
6. Don’t use newspaper headlines at the beginning doesn’t work visually.
7. Judge Desai – first name add in?
8. All the SD material needs to be in a squeeze back – with a thin white frame.
9. We need more from the Minister on the extent to which there are phones in prison and what they are doing
10. You can cut down the section on their parole it was long
11. Please can you make sure you are showing us Frans in the old images you are using? We think you are zooming in on the wrong guy – please check!
12. Don’t show Alfred Ramphiri name
13. Please disguise Joyce Reed voice
14. Need subtitles on the mother – say we are not naming the mom? We see MRS Reed’s name in the letter if you are hiding her name...
15. You are naming Lisa in the whatsapp chats please take her name out
16. + book was reprinted so many times? Find out how many
17. The story has to be 10 mins. Apologies for the implication that it may go at 12 – that was only an option if GM agreed


From: Laura Byrne
Sent: 20 April 2015 01:37 PM
To: Amalia Christoforou
Cc: Michael Duffett
Subject: Alison Botha viewing: my comments

Hi Ami and Michael

Michael – I really enjoyed the story, I think it’s come together so well and we’ll have something both important and sensational to show on Sunday!

I just had a couple of accuracy points to make. I’ve elaborated below, but they concern:
1. The picture of the two attackers
2. The throat slitting
3. The Satanism
4. The parole hearing date

First and most importantly, are we absolutely sure that we’re zooming in on the right face in that photo of Frans and Theuns drinking juice in the court during the trial? (I’ve copied it below).



We keep zooming in on the guy on the right, but I have a strong feeling Frans is the one on the left. See this photo below (the photographer identified Frans du Toit as the guy in the centre).



...AND he looks more like this picture too. Obviously if Alison has identified the guy on the right as Frans, that’s different – just wanted to check.


Secondly, I think it was Kruger who first started to cut Alison’s throat. See the below from the sentence (Beskuldigde no 1 is Frans du Toit and Beskuldigde no 2 is Theuns Kruger)





Third: we say that they claimed to be under the influence of Satan. Would it be safer/more accurate to say they were practising Satanists who claimed to be under the influence of an incubus? Du Toit claimed he had been possessed by an incubus that ordered him to rape women and they thought if they both raped a woman, the incubus would pass onto Kruger. There was a lot of talk about the incubus in the trial. See below:


Finally, as Michael is trying to establish, the parole hearing may have been delayed even further – this is something we’ll have to confirm and/or allow for in the script. Maybe by saying that when it came up the first time in 2013, it was decided that the hearing would be delayed until October 2015 – that bypasses any change that is happening in the date now.

Then it’s just very important as we said to remove all mention of Uga or Joyce, and to disguise Joyce’s voice.

Viewing 2
Duncan, Laura, Wynand, Amalia – GM needs to watch

Thank you for making the changes we asked for.

LEGAL
You have covered all we spoke about yesterday and taken out what Dario suggesetd re Alison’s comments. Its fine. It’s now just the right of reply – have we given him enough time? We don’t know how difficult it is for him to get a reply out – he has Dario’s email and a phone number. If he is not allowed access to the internet how does he respond and a phone call might be easy/hard. There is a risk he will say he only had 3 days and he wasn’t able to respond in time. MIKE: the interesting thing is that he is positing on FB today. Laura has screen grabbed this. George says we go with it anyway we did ask this earlier today and he says we can use. Duncan says there is a low risk.

GENERAL
• Rather use our CB background on Alison recap where she says please don’t kill me, don’t use the footage in the background. Please do this both times you go to her for recap. Also same where you recap before Presiding Judge Jansen.
• Please don’t use music over the interviews.
• The audio on Jansen has a buzzing sound in the background – what’s the matter there?
• Where you show us Du Toit and Kruger in the parole section in the photo where they are together drinking orange juice please darken the screen a little on one side alternately when you refer to each one so viewers know which is which.
• Please don’t use online headlines in the section on parole – there are two sections where you do this. IOL
• Introduce Judge Siraj Desai also using his first name. and put in his correct title
• Highlight “yes I am with Frans” clearly for viewers pull it out towards viewers
• Please pull out on screen Alison’s words in the letter to correctional services
• Say Du Toit will have to explain these when his parole hearing...
• You cant say fucking...
• Don’t show the letter we sent to Frans.
• Say that we made several attempts to reach Frans for comment through the Grootvlei prison authorities who despite this never came back to us. And we then tried to contact Frans directly and delivered a letter to him at the prison which he signed for. But he never took up our request for an interview.
• You say he was sentenced for the ‘raping’ – its ‘rape’
• You use the word LIFERS – rather use inmates serving life sentences
• You say Frans was sentenced to 3 life sentences for rape. Take out ‘for rape’. End it at three life sentences
• There are still names in the letter to the prison authorities... hide MR MARREN name in the letter.
• You will disguise Joyce Reed’s voice in the final mix
• We change from Judge Desai saying ‘its a bit more complicated with them’ and you go to Zabo can you segway that better and strap him again – you are citing Desai and what he says and then putting in Zabo.
• Apparently the minister clarifies that they are only supposed to have access to the internet for e-learning – please put that in as it clarifies that there is no way he should be on FBook.
• When can we see your promos?

Press Release:


Alison Botha
Two decades ago, Alison Botha was abducted, raped, stabbed more than thirty times, almost decapitated and left for dead. Defying the odds, she survived. Her story has gripped the nation ever since. While Alison now faces the possibility of parole for her attackers - who were sentenced to life imprisonment - a sinister discovery has shed light on the activity of one of her attackers behind prison bars. Carte Blanche investigates.
Watch our promo.


Script:


It was a crime so shocking that it still remains in the nations consciousness 20 years later.


LINK: IT WAS A MOMENT THAT ALISON BOTHA WILL NEVER FORGET. JUST AFTER MIDNIGHT ON THE 18TH OF DECEMBER 1994, SHE ARRIVED HOME IN CENTRAL PORT ELIZABETH AND WAS CONFRONTED WAS CONFRONTED BY A KNIFE WIELDING FRANS DU TOIT.

Frans du Toit who was already out on bail for the abduction and rape of two other young women, one of whom was pregnant, climbed behind the wheel of her car and together with Theuns Kruger drove her to secluded spot in Port Elizabeth, where they took turns in raping her and then proceeded to strangle her.

Alison: I looked up and I said please don’t kill me, he said sorry, and it was very quick that I passed out. That I lost consciousness.

The pair dragged her from the car and she was stabbed more than 30 times in the abdomen. Then her throat was slashed multiple times. They left her for dead. Clinging onto life Alison started to crawl towards the road. She used her discarded shirt to hold in her intestines.

Alison: I actually had to hold my head up. The one muscle on this side was actually cut through, so the head flopped right back and so I actually had to hold it up so I could see.

Alison was rescued by a passing motorist who rushed her to hospital. Doctors say it was a miracle she survived.

After their arrest Du Toit and Kruger were sent to a state forensic psychiatrist to determine if they were fit to stand trial. Proffesor Tuviah Zabow fond them fit to stand trial.

John. What was you response to the detail that you were hearing?
Zabow: I was quite distressed at the intensity of the violence.
John: And that is saying something, given your experience.
Zabow: This is significant and the sadistic element which became evident.

On 12th of June 1995 the trial began. The presiding judge was Chris Jansen, now retired.

Judge: Alison who was a pretty young lady with this terrible scar on her neck when she came into court, immediately made a very good impression on me.

Kruger and Detroit who admitted to the crimes claimed to be under the influence of evil spirits. Du Toit however claimed to have been set free from them following an exorcism while awaiting trial and yet Chris Jansen found his attitude in court alarming.

Judge: What a strange guy he was. He always starred at me with some hatred and with a sort of challenging attitude as if he believed that nothing was going to happen to him, and even when he gave evidence completely without any emotion.

Chris Jansen found Du Toit guilty for the rape of Alison and two other women.


LINK: FRANS DUTOIT REVIVED 3 LIFE SENTENCES FOR VARIOUS CHARGES INCLUDING INDECENT ASSAULT, RAPE, KIDNAPPING, ROBBERY WITH AGGRAVATING CIRCUMSTANCES AND ATTEMPTED MURDER. THEUNS KRUGER RECEIVED ONE LIFE SENTENCE AND 25 YEARS.

And that was for participating in Alison’s attack and one other.

John: It was clear that you didn’t want these two to ever get back into society. Is that right?
Judge: That is completely true.
John: Why?
Judge: Because I really thought that they were a danger to society.

In his sentencing the judge made it clear that men should remain in prison for the rest of their natural lives. He ordered a copy of the sentence to be forwarded to their prison and the minister of correctional services in case they were considered for parole

LINK: AFTER HER COURT CASE AND HAVING UNDERGONE THERAPY, ALISON WAS ASKED TO GIVE A NUMBER OF TALKS ABOUT HER ORDEAL, WHICH SHE FOUND HELPED WITH THE HEALING PROCESS. SHE ALSO WROTE AN ACCLAIMED BOOK AND BECAME A MOTIVATIONAL SPEAKER IN WHICH SHE ENCOURAGED OTHER PEOPLE TO DRAW ON THEIR OWN RESILIENCE IN OVERCOMING CHALLENGES AND TRAUMA.

Now Alison has to face a new chapter in her life.

John: Alison 20 years down the line, how you doing?
Alison: It’s fine, I can’t believe its 20 years since the attack and you guys covered that, things are fine, I am a single mom and happy, still do my talks and share about my story and hopefully inspire people with it.
John: Do you ever think back to that night? Do you ever spend time thinking about your attackers?
Alison: I’ve come to realize you never get over it. It’s something that you learn to live with and some days it’s harder than others to be honest.

Recent events have left her shaken.

Alison: I have been struggling in the last few years and a friend of mine actually pinpointed for me the other day from the point from when I heard that he would be applying for parole.

Recent legislation stipulates that all inmates sentenced to live before 2004 are eligible for parole after serving at least 13 years and 4 months. Du Toit and Kruger had served 17 years since their sentencing in 1995. Their case was heard in 2013 but was postponed for reconsideration to October this year.

Judge Desai: the decision to release an offender is a difficult one. It’s difficult simply because the person has been sentenced to life in prison, has offended and has offended seriously sufficiently so to get a life sentence.

Judge Siraj Desai heads up a team of experts who consider parole applications of prisoners serving life. The team make their recommendation to the minister of justice who has final say.

Judge: On the other hand the person has matured in prison, has been well behaved, the psychologist says that he is rehabilitated, the social worker say he is rehabilitated, then it’s a safe bet to release him on parole, and now days to be released on parole subject to electronic monitoring.

The judge added that certain types of sexual offenders present a more complicated picture, for example hardened pedophiles. We asked professor Tuviah Zabow about the rehabilitation prospects of Du Toit who had been sentenced for three violent rapes.

Zabow: How does one reevaluate his sexual orientation and his sexual gratification?
John: And of course in prison he won’t be around women?
Zabow: Well it’s very difficult to assess because we are not putting him out to test.

Another issue has emerged. It seems contrary to prison regulations, du Toit is having a relationship from within Grootvlei Correctional Centre and that’s via Facebook.

LINK: OUT OF THE BLUE ALISON RECEIVED AN EMAIL FROM THE USA, BEGGING FOR HELP. A WOMAN CLAIMED THAT HE DAUGHTER WAS HAVING AN ONLINE RELATIONSHIP WITH FRANS DU TOIT.


She had gained access to her daughter’s private face book messages. It’s alleged that Frans du Toit has several facebook profiles easily accessible to the pubic.She tracked down Alison and emailed her

John: So what was that, a cry for help?
Allison: I think so, she was just desperate – she didn’t know what else to do?

She told Alison that she had complained to Correctional Services but had not heard back from them. But it seems that some type of action was taken, judging from private exchanges allegedly from du Toit to her daughter Sabrina on facebook.

“for three hears I have never had a problem living with a phone in prison, that was until your mother reported me and I started being searched around the clock, I have lost thousands since then in lost items and bribes.”

We contacted Sabrina but she preferred not to comment. She did say that she was with Frans. Her mother agreed to speak to us.

Mother: when I talked to her, she said she loves him. And she believes in her heart that he has changed.

The mother confirmed that her daughter was spanning to visit South Africa soon.

John: I understand that there have been a couple of occasions in the past when she has made it to the airport in the states?
Mother: She is a single mother. Her son, he was very upset, he did not want to go, so he caused a really bad temper at the airport, so she had to cancel because of it.

John: So Alison when Joyce contacted you what is it that she wanted you to do? Did she make that clear?
Alison: I don’t think she even knew but it was more what can you do? So the only thing I could think of doing and what I did do was write to the prison services. The same ones that I had dealt with at the time of the first parole hearing.

Alison complained to correctional services about du Toits alleged cellphone usage. She also wrote, I am desperate to know that he will be stopped from manipulating and destroying this young girls life.

It’s illegal for prisoners to have access to cell hones and according to media reports, it appears be rampant, with many prisoners updating their face book pages. She asked that her complaint be kept strictly confidential.

Minister: Cellphones are contraband. They are not allowed period and anybody who has access to a cellphone does so illegally.

Minister Masutha added that some prisoners do have access to computers but that was only for e-learning.

Minister: It’s allowed under strict supervision of the tutors.

Alison asked that her complaint be kept strictly confidential and that “she never be revealed as the source of the information.” She didn’t hear back from the authorities and what has made her furious is that her email seems to have been shown to du Toit judging from this alleged Facebook exchange between him and Sabrina.

“No I read Alison email, someone in your family has been in contact with her recently.”

Alison: I don’t feel safe. How do I feel now and who do I contact? I can’t trust anyone. I don’t know who in that system can I… so I’ve come to you. I don’t like doing it this way but what else do I do to find out what is actually going on?

Alison has read some of the Facebook exchanges with Sabrina which she finds concerning. Du Toit will most likely have to explain these when his hearing comes up later this year.

“Sharon got a friendly warning a week or so ago. Ok maybe not so friendly, the boys did have some fun with her…

“David knows I am bad, he does just not know how fxxxxxg bad I am, if Sharon wanted to tell him some secret, I think she would tell him about 28, and my authority in the system of 28, and what 28 do.”

Of course 28 is the name of the gang in the prison system.

Alison finds these messages chilling.

Alison: Now the facebook, that’s one step from me or from the world.
This is not someone who stole something, this is a person ho stabbed me 37 times in my abdomen, that’s what he is capable of.

We made several attempts to get reach du Toit for comment through the Grootvlei authorities but they didn’t respond. We then delivered a letter to him in prison, which he signed for. He has not yet taken up our request for an interview or provided feedback. Grootvlei Correctional Centre too did not respond to our request for an interview. We wanted to know if they had shown alison’s confidential letter to du Toit. We brought that up with the minister who expressed deep concern that there may have been a breach of confidentiality.

Minister: If there is negligence including gross negligence then corrective measures would have to be taken against the person concerned and if it borders on a criminal offence that should be dealt with as such.

Defying the odds, she survived. Her story has gripped the nation ever since. While Alison now faces the possibility of parole for her attackers - who were sentenced to life imprisonment - a sinister discovery has shed light on the activity of one of her attackers behind prison bars. Carte Blanche investigates. Watch our promo. Script: It was a crime so shocking that it still remains in the nations consciousness 20 years later. LINK: IT WAS A MOMENT THAT ALISON BOTHA WILL NEVER FORGET. JUST AFTER MIDNIGHT ON THE 18TH OF DECEMBER 1994, SHE ARRIVED HOME IN CENTRAL PORT ELIZABETH AND WAS CONFRONTED WAS CONFRONTED BY A KNIFE WIELDING FRANS DU TOIT. Frans du Toit who was already out on bail for the abduction and rape of two other young women, one of whom was pregnant, climbed behind the wheel of her car and together with Theuns Kruger drove her to secluded spot in Port Elizabeth, where they took turns in raping her and then proceeded to strangle her. Alison: I looked up and I said please don’t kill me, he said sorry, and it was very quick that I passed out. That I lost consciousness. The pair dragged her from the car and she was stabbed more than 30 times in the abdomen. Then her throat was slashed multiple times. They left her for dead. Clinging onto life Alison started to crawl towards the road. She used her discarded shirt to hold in her intestines. Alison: I actually had to hold my head up. The one muscle on this side was actually cut through, so the head flopped right back and so I actually had to hold it up so I could see. Alison was rescued by a passing motorist who rushed her to hospital. Doctors say it was a miracle she survived. After their arrest Du Toit and Kruger were sent to a state forensic psychiatrist to determine if they were fit to stand trial. Proffesor Tuviah Zabow fond them fit to stand trial. John. What was you response to the detail that you were hearing? Zabow: I was quite distressed at the intensity of the violence. John: And that is saying something, given your experience. Zabow: This is significant and the sadistic element which became evident. On 12th of June 1995 the trial began. The presiding judge was Chris Jansen, now retired. Judge: Alison who was a pretty young lady with this terrible scar on her neck when she came into court, immediately made a very good impression on me. Kruger and Detroit who admitted to the crimes claimed to be under the influence of evil spirits. Du Toit however claimed to have been set free from them following an exorcism while awaiting trial and yet Chris Jansen found his attitude in court alarming. Judge: What a strange guy he was. He always starred at me with some hatred and with a sort of challenging attitude as if he believed that nothing was going to happen to him, and even when he gave evidence completely without any emotion. Chris Jansen found Du Toit guilty for the rape of Alison and two other women. LINK: FRANS DUTOIT REVIVED 3 LIFE SENTENCES FOR VARIOUS CHARGES INCLUDING INDECENT ASSAULT, RAPE, KIDNAPPING, ROBBERY WITH AGGRAVATING CIRCUMSTANCES AND ATTEMPTED MURDER. THEUNS KRUGER RECEIVED ONE LIFE SENTENCE AND 25 YEARS. And that was for participating in Alison’s attack and one other. John: It was clear that you didn’t want these two to ever get back into society. Is that right? Judge: That is completely true. John: Why? Judge: Because I really thought that they were a danger to society. In his sentencing the judge made it clear that men should remain in prison for the rest of their natural lives. He ordered a copy of the sentence to be forwarded to their prison and the minister of correctional services in case they were considered for parole LINK: AFTER HER COURT CASE AND HAVING UNDERGONE THERAPY, ALISON WAS ASKED TO GIVE A NUMBER OF TALKS ABOUT HER ORDEAL, WHICH SHE FOUND HELPED WITH THE HEALING PROCESS. SHE ALSO WROTE AN ACCLAIMED BOOK AND BECAME A MOTIVATIONAL SPEAKER IN WHICH SHE ENCOURAGED OTHER PEOPLE TO DRAW ON THEIR OWN RESILIENCE IN OVERCOMING CHALLENGES AND TRAUMA. Now Alison has to face a new chapter in her life. John: Alison 20 years down the line, how you doing? Alison: It’s fine, I can’t believe its 20 years since the attack and you guys covered that, things are fine, I am a single mom and happy, still do my talks and share about my story and hopefully inspire people with it. John: Do you ever think back to that night? Do you ever spend time thinking about your attackers? Alison: I’ve come to realize you never get over it. It’s something that you learn to live with and some days it’s harder than others to be honest. Recent events have left her shaken. Alison: I have been struggling in the last few years and a friend of mine actually pinpointed for me the other day from the point from when I heard that he would be applying for parole. Recent legislation stipulates that all inmates sentenced to live before 2004 are eligible for parole after serving at least 13 years and 4 months. Du Toit and Kruger had served 17 years since their sentencing in 1995. Their case was heard in 2013 but was postponed for reconsideration to October this year. Judge Desai: the decision to release an offender is a difficult one. It’s difficult simply because the person has been sentenced to life in prison, has offended and has offended seriously sufficiently so to get a life sentence. Judge Siraj Desai heads up a team of experts who consider parole applications of prisoners serving life. The team make their recommendation to the minister of justice who has final say. Judge: On the other hand the person has matured in prison, has been well behaved, the psychologist says that he is rehabilitated, the social worker say he is rehabilitated, then it’s a safe bet to release him on parole, and now days to be released on parole subject to electronic monitoring. The judge added that certain types of sexual offenders present a more complicated picture, for example hardened pedophiles. We asked professor Tuviah Zabow about the rehabilitation prospects of Du Toit who had been sentenced for three violent rapes. Zabow: How does one reevaluate his sexual orientation and his sexual gratification? John: And of course in prison he won’t be around women? Zabow: Well it’s very difficult to assess because we are not putting him out to test. Another issue has emerged. It seems contrary to prison regulations, du Toit is having a relationship from within Grootvlei Correctional Centre and that’s via Facebook. LINK: OUT OF THE BLUE ALISON RECEIVED AN EMAIL FROM THE USA, BEGGING FOR HELP. A WOMAN CLAIMED THAT HE DAUGHTER WAS HAVING AN ONLINE RELATIONSHIP WITH FRANS DU TOIT. She had gained access to her daughter’s private face book messages. It’s alleged that Frans du Toit has several facebook profiles easily accessible to the pubic.She tracked down Alison and emailed her John: So what was that, a cry for help? Allison: I think so, she was just desperate – she didn’t know what else to do? She told Alison that she had complained to Correctional Services but had not heard back from them. But it seems that some type of action was taken, judging from private exchanges allegedly from du Toit to her daughter Sabrina on facebook. “for three hears I have never had a problem living with a phone in prison, that was until your mother reported me and I started being searched around the clock, I have lost thousands since then in lost items and bribes.” We contacted Sabrina but she preferred not to comment. She did say that she was with Frans. Her mother agreed to speak to us. Mother: when I talked to her, she said she loves him. And she believes in her heart that he has changed. The mother confirmed that her daughter was spanning to visit South Africa soon. John: I understand that there have been a couple of occasions in the past when she has made it to the airport in the states? Mother: She is a single mother. Her son, he was very upset, he did not want to go, so he caused a really bad temper at the airport, so she had to cancel because of it. John: So Alison when Joyce contacted you what is it that she wanted you to do? Did she make that clear? Alison: I don’t think she even knew but it was more what can you do? So the only thing I could think of doing and what I did do was write to the prison services. The same ones that I had dealt with at the time of the first parole hearing. Alison complained to correctional services about du Toits alleged cellphone usage. She also wrote, I am desperate to know that he will be stopped from manipulating and destroying this young girls life. It’s illegal for prisoners to have access to cell hones and according to media reports, it appears be rampant, with many prisoners updating their face book pages. She asked that her complaint be kept strictly confidential. Minister: Cellphones are contraband. They are not allowed period and anybody who has access to a cellphone does so illegally. Minister Masutha added that some prisoners do have access to computers but that was only for e-learning. Minister: It’s allowed under strict supervision of the tutors. Alison asked that her complaint be kept strictly confidential and that “she never be revealed as the source of the information.” She didn’t hear back from the authorities and what has made her furious is that her email seems to have been shown to du Toit judging from this alleged Facebook exchange between him and Sabrina. “No I read Alison email, someone in your family has been in contact with her recently.” Alison: I don’t feel safe. How do I feel now and who do I contact? I can’t trust anyone. I don’t know who in that system can I… so I’ve come to you. I don’t like doing it this way but what else do I do to find out what is actually going on? Alison has read some of the Facebook exchanges with Sabrina which she finds concerning. Du Toit will most likely have to explain these when his hearing comes up later this year. “Sharon got a friendly warning a week or so ago. Ok maybe not so friendly, the boys did have some fun with her… “David knows I am bad, he does just not know how fxxxxxg bad I am, if Sharon wanted to tell him some secret, I think she would tell him about 28, and my authority in the system of 28, and what 28 do.” Of course 28 is the name of the gang in the prison system. Alison finds these messages chilling. Alison: Now the facebook, that’s one step from me or from the world. This is not someone who stole something, this is a person ho stabbed me 37 times in my abdomen, that’s what he is capable of. We made several attempts to get reach du Toit for comment through the Grootvlei authorities but they didn’t respond. We then delivered a letter to him in prison, which he signed for. He has not yet taken up our request for an interview or provided feedback. Grootvlei Correctional Centre too did not respond to our request for an interview. We wanted to know if they had shown alison’s confidential letter to du Toit. We brought that up with the minister who expressed deep concern that there may have been a breach of confidentiality. Minister: If there is negligence including gross negligence then corrective measures would have to be taken against the person concerned and if it borders on a criminal offence that should be dealt with as such.

metadata.Summary: Many viewers will remember the story 20 years ago of the bravery of Alison Botha who was raped, stabbed repeatedly and had her throat so severely cut that she was almost decapitated. Her rapist, along with an accomplice, who was out on bail already for two other rapes, was sentenced to three life sentences with the judge wanting him never to see the light of day again. Such was the resilience of Alison that she survived, recovered and went on to become a motivational speaker. Now a film is about to be made on her and it was during the research for this film that some rather disturbing news has emerged... • Frans, her rapist, is having an internet based relationship with someone on the outside. • The filmmaker was horrified to find that a warder of his started to communicate with her via Whatsapp. • Facebook exchanges show that wardens know about Frans's access to the internet/Facebook and chat rooms. • It seems that this man may be up for parole. • When Alison complained to authorities about Frans having internet access and asked for her complaint to be kept confidential, it seems that the prison head went straight to Frans with her complaint. Alison is furious about this and her name now is being thrown around by Frans in his Facebook exchanges.
metadata.Further information: The story is about a recap of the brutal experience suffered by Alison. Her inspirational tale moved a local filmmaker who has decided to make a film about her. In her research, and when she contacted all the role players, she discovered everything that is written above. Alison feels compromised. It seems that correctional services have acted with extreme stupidity. One of the questions we need to look at once again during this program is the possibility that those convicted of the most heinous crimes could be getting parole. A question we must ask, is there any crime committed that is so horrific and evil that there is no chance of them ever leaving prison. Frans would seem to fit this picture. The story will leave the viewer feeling this... woman who survives her horrific ordeal and manages to rebuild her life. She now is compromised by the inept actions of correctional services.
